answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by staking reputation on a trellis of verifiable work: each identity must first complete costly, independently checkable tasks before it can harvest any nectar, such as fees or rewards. A newcomer that merely repeats a whisper of someone else's output earns nothing, because peers attest only original, timestamped work tied to a single key. Creating thousands of fake identities then costs thousands of times the compute and time, while one honest agent pays once.
